skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 gave the full warning before any substantive question: counsel represents the Committee and company, not Fastow, and cannot give him legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 said privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned, including to the government, without his consent. T5 confirmed back.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explained the structure, ground rules on speculation and estimates, asked for complete answers, and asked whether the process was acceptable.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 had him restate who was represented and who controls privilege, and T2 and T6 invited questions and checked understanding.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T374 asked for anything to add and gave confidentiality, record-keeping and no-contact reminders, but next steps were only 'we may follow up'.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as T16 'Tell me everything you remember' and T44 let the witness walk through LJM1, Chewco, and the Raptor and Foundation matters before narrowing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moved sensibly from role and reporting lines (T8-T15) to transactions, then to specific approvals, payments and documents.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear, but some are compound or framed as 'help me understand how' prompts, such as T262 and T306.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Stayed neutral and polite under pushback at T20 to T23 and T252 to T253, and kept control of the agenda throughout.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Pressed specific statements such as high teens at T241 and optimistically at T252, then pivoted into the Foundation and Southampton investment at T120 to T125.

skills.name: Material Facts

skills.name: Other Sources

skills.name: Other Evidence

Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?
Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
Moved from the expected Raptor return to actual LJM2 returns, then narrowed step by step to an estimate.
Asked a loaded question about whether the Board should have known LJM2 returns were several times what it had been told.
So that I have it right: you may have been kept informed of the buyout figure, but you did not negotiate it. Is that correct?

area_evidence.area: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
How certain are you of that figure?
Fairly certain it was around four and a half million.
How sure are you of that figure?
The minutes record you saying there had been "tremendous utilization" of Raptor I. Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.
I was describing demand from the business units. I may have put it optimistically.
Not much. He was fine with it.
Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to "Andy," refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
Michael kept me informed about things generally. Being informed isn't the same as negotiating.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
Without handing anything over today, what do those notes and emails cover, and where are they kept?
I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
They don't mention Michael, which fits my memory that it didn't come up.
Asked what the witness remembered about Southampton Place before showing the partnership agreement.
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
Who prepared it, and where was it kept?
I'd like to show you LJM2's October 2000 report to its investors. Do you recognize it?
It lists returns of 193, 278, and 2,500 percent on three of the Raptor transactions. Are those the figures LJM2 reported to its investors?
I'd like to show you an April 2001 communication to LJM2's investors. Do you recognize it?
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
That's correct.

missed_chances.description: The witness said Skilling was 'fine with' the roughly $10 million buyout figure. This key lead on who knew about the payment was never followed up.
missed_chances.question: What exactly did Mr. Skilling say when you told him the deal was done at about $10 million, and did he ask how that figure was reached?

missed_chances.description: The witness said Skilling signed off on some LJM deals, but the interviewer never asked which deals or what Skilling reviewed before signing.
missed_chances.question: Which LJM deals did Mr. Skilling sign off on, and what did he review before signing?

tips: When a witness says a senior officer was told or approved something, ask: what exactly did they say, and did they ask how the figure was reached?
Before accepting that controls were adequate, ask: which specific LJM2 transactions did Causey and Buy actually review, and what did the approval sheets show about when they were signed?
